summary: O-027 is fixed by raising the window's minimum height. MinHeight is now 600, the same as its default height, so the window can no longer be dragged to a height where the outcome row's 316/328 px floor pushes the results list or the outcome's own lists off the window. B-007 now runs its four endings twice: at the default 880x600, and again at the window's own MinHeight. For the second run, a new hook `size` mode (and FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT=1 for use with watch and expand) sets Window.Height to Window.MinHeight before the scan starts. Measured: with MinHeight 400 the MinHeight run fails (TopLevelList 0 px, LargestFilesList out of view). With a trial MinHeight of 580 the two opened endings lose the results list (0 px). At 600 every list is in view in all eight runs. The XAML comment no longer claims the layout works at every window size: it says the floor fits from about 580 px of height up, gives the default width as a condition, and records that the minimum width of 560 is not covered. docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md is updated to match.

files.why: O-027. Window MinHeight goes from 400 to 600, the default height. The Grid comment is corrected: the floor fits only from about 580 px of height up, so the window's MinHeight is 600. The claim that no panel pushes another off the window now holds only at the default width and with one line of drive buttons. The comment also states plainly that the MinWidth of 560 is not covered.

Adds a `size` mode and the FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT=1 variable (watch and expand only). Both register a Window Loaded class handler before the window loads; it sets Height to MinHeight ahead of the window's own Loaded handler, which starts the scan. The hook logs 'sized height=n minHeight=n', and `size` mode also logs 'acted mode=size'. Only `size` mode waits on the UI thread to check the registration was in time, because that wait made expand's handler register too late (measured on the first try). Header docs are updated.

B-007 now repeats its four endings (Completed and Cancelled, unreadable list closed and opened) at the window's MinHeight through size/FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT. Each of those runs asserts, via a new CheckSized helper, that the hook sized the window to its MinHeight. It also asserts that LargestFilesList, UnreadableExpander, UnreadableList (when opened) and TopLevelList are all inView. FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT is added to $HookVariables, and the B-007 header says what it now covers.
The window section now says the outcome floor fits only from about 580 px of height up, so the window's MinHeight is 600, and that B-007 measures the layout at the default size and at the MinHeight.

obligations.how: I took the 'raise the window's MinHeight' option, the smaller of the two changes the disposition allowed: MainWindow.xaml MinHeight is now 600, up from 400. B-007 now runs all four endings at the window's MinHeight through the new hook `size` mode and FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT=1. At 600 every run passes: LargestFilesList is 47.9–99.96 px, UnreadableList 42.8–51.3 px when opened, and TopLevelList 19.26–31.26 px, all in view. With MinHeight 400 the same runs failed (TopLevelList 0 px, LargestFilesList and UnreadableExpander out of view). A trial MinHeight of 580 passed the closed endings (TopLevelList 11.26 px) but failed both opened ones (0 px). The comment at MainWindow.xaml:37-49 now states what holds: the floor fits from about 580 px up, the guarantee is at the default width with one line of drive buttons, and the MinWidth of 560 is not covered.

deviations: MinHeight is 600, not the smallest height at which the four endings pass. The measured zero point is about 581 px: a trial MinHeight of 580 left TopLevelList at 0 px in both opened endings, and TopLevelList shrinks one pixel per pixel of height below 600. Anything between 581 and 599 would keep the results list 'in view' at under 19 px, down to a fraction of a pixel. That height also depends on the pickers staying on one line. 600 is the default height, where the opened endings keep 19 px and the closed ones 31 px. As a result the window can no longer be made shorter than its default.

Only `size` mode checks, with a UI-thread Invoke, that its handler registered before the window loaded. With FSA_HOOK_MINHEIGHT ahead of watch or expand the hook skips that check: the first try measured that the Invoke waits until the window has loaded, which made expand's handler register too late and refuse. For those modes a missing 'sized' line is what shows the sizing was late, and B-007's CheckSized asserts that line.
not_built: The window's minimum width is not covered: it was measured, not fixed. At 560x600 (MinWidth by default height; Width was changed temporarily and restored, hash-checked), the Cancelled ending with the unreadable list opened clips LargestFilesList (24 px, not in view). The Completed ending with the list opened keeps only 3.3 px of TopLevelList. O-027 is about height only, so I did not change MinWidth. The comment at MainWindow.xaml says this plainly instead of claiming it.
follow_ups: Window width: at the allowed MinWidth of 560, a stopped scan's texts wrap past the outcome floor, and with its unreadable folders open the largest-files list is clipped (measured at 560x600: LargestFilesList 24 px, not in view). Raise MinWidth, derive the floor from the actual texts, or settle it with the open window-size question (larger default, tabs, side by side) in design-slice.

The results list's share depends on the pickers' height. A second line of drive buttons (more drives, or a narrower window) comes straight out of TopLevelList's 19–31 px at 600 px height, and the report reads more room when a fast scan ends before the drive buttons have loaded. A layout that does not depend on the pickers, or a report that waits for them, would make B-007's margins independent of the machine.

tests.note: Failed as intended. The default-size half passed. At MinHeight 400 the closed endings gave TopLevelList 0 px, LargestFilesList and UnreadableExpander not in view, and mid-scan list height 0. The opened runs at 400 failed because expand refused ('window loaded before the hook could watch'), a hook ordering bug, fixed next.

tests.note: All six non-expand runs passed. The two opened MinHeight runs failed on the hook: size's UI-thread Invoke delayed expand's registration until after the window loaded. After the fix only size mode does that check.

Exe republished at the start. 25 cases passed (C-001 to C-014, O-016, L-001 to L-003, B-001 to B-007). N-001 to N-004 were not run: they change SMB mappings. B-007 at MinHeight: 'sized height=600 minHeight=600'; LargestFilesList 47.9–99.96 px, UnreadableList 42.8–51.3 px, TopLevelList 19.26–31.26 px, all in view.
Re-run on the final source after a comment-only XAML edit: all eight runs passed, and every MinHeight run logged sized height=600 minHeight=600.
H-001 and H-002 passed with the changed hook.
